`119` should return note **#119** (and the same for todos), not just items whose
title/body text happens to contain "119". Today panopt search is plain SQL
`LIKE '%query%'` over `title`/`body` only — the numeric `id` column is selected for
ordering but never matched against. So a user who knows an item by its `#N` reference
can't jump to it from search.

**Decisions (confirmed with user):**

  single leading `#`, so `#119` works too. Title/body substring matching is unchanged

predicate when the query parses as a number.

call into these two core functions unchanged, so the new behavior propagates to MCP and
the search dialog automatically — no edits needed there or in `panopt-tool-surface`.

### 1. Add a small private helper (near the search fns in `state.rs`)

Parses a query into an exact id when it looks like one: trim whitespace, strip a single
optional leading `#`, then `u64::from_str`. Returns `None` for non-numeric queries.

```rust

/// `119` or `#119`) is treated as an exact id lookup against the unified
/// per-project id, so `#N` references are reachable from search. Non-numeric
/// queries return `None` and fall through to plain title/body matching.
fn query_as_id(query: &str) -> Option<u64> {
    query.trim().strip_prefix('#').unwrap_or(query.trim()).parse().ok()
}
```

group also matches the exact id when the query is numeric. Keep the existing
title/body `LIKE` and the existing placeholder-numbering pattern (`binds.len() + 1`):

```rust

    let pat = format!("%{}%", q.to_lowercase());
    let n = binds.len() + 1;
    binds.push(Box::new(pat));
    let mut clause = format!("LOWER(title) LIKE ?{0} OR LOWER(body) LIKE ?{0}", n);
    if let Some(id) = query_as_id(q) {
        let m = binds.len() + 1;
        binds.push(Box::new(id as i64));
        clause.push_str(&format!(" OR id = ?{m}"));
    }
    sql.push_str(&format!(" AND ({clause})"));

matches the exact id.

2. **Build/clippy** — run the `verify-all` skill (workspace + wasm plugin), or `cargo test -p panopt-core` plus `cargo clippy -p panopt-core`.
3. **End-to-end via MCP** — after `just refresh`, call `note_search`/`todo_search` (or the `panopt search` TUI) with a known id and confirm the item appears.

- `crates/panopt-core/src/state.rs` — `note_search` (451-497), `todo_search` (1049-1112), new `query_as_id` helper, tests (`mod tests` at 1655+).

Parses a query into an exact id when it looks like one: trim whitespace, strip a single

/// `119` or `#119`) is treated as an exact id lookup against the unified

fn query_as_id(query: &str) -> Option<u64> {

}
